title: The Spiritual Zion and the Davidic Promise
english: Observe, examining iniquities; for if he were to do this, no one would stand. For all have strayed, all have sinned. Therefore, since no one stands before the judgment from you, there is need of the propitiation from you, being propitiated for the salvation of all.

And what is the propitiation, the Savior? John writes: 'And if anyone sins, we have an advocate with the Father, a righteous Lord Jesus Christ' (1 John 2:1); and he himself is the propitiation for our sins, not only concerning ours but also concerning the sins of the world. But also Paul: 'For all have sinned and fall short of the glory of God, being justified freely by his grace through the redemption that is in Christ Jesus, whom God put forward as a propitiation through faith in his blood' (Romans 3:23-25), and the following. A symbol of this propitiation was constructed in the law, concerning which also now the one praying to God says: 'That from you is the propitiation'; from you, as a generation from the only good Father, is the propitiation. Not every rational creature needs, not with a god to be upheld, observing the iniquities of each of the created ones.

Always and at all times it is necessary to hope in the Lord, not only the one standing openly but also the one standing in gloom. From the morning watch, the one with the bright things present, and until night, the one with the dreary and darker things surrounding; and what is from the morning watch, the rising of the true light and making the beginning of a mental day, the discerning mind, Israel, called by the Hebrew voice, let him hope in the Lord (Ps 129:6-8), expecting from him an addition of the bright things and a deliverance from the gloomy things, what is from him as in a fountain and from him the mercy which those hoping in him need; but also much redemption from him, the propitiation from him is not another; for he himself from all iniquities will redeem him. For even if the iniquities of Israel are many, from all he will redeem him.

David, having perfected gentleness, says the following: 'Remembering me,' he says, 'upon these things you will give me an inheritance, the land of the gentle' (Ps 131:1). And those with these priests, not by chance, but they shall rejoice, they shall rejoice, of the only perfect and from the beginning rejoicing, from the most perfect rejoicing of this thing. And it is possible that the...

The person and the saint are the same, though distinguished by relations, for one is priest and the other is a saint of God, being the same in substance as the subject. Who is the cause of them putting on righteousness and rejoicing? It is David, the holy one, who is capable by hand. For the Lord brought forth for David his servant. He who became God's servant according to the flesh from the seed of David, having taken the form of the servant, emptied himself.

Understand thus [Ps 131:10b]: intending by your grace to shine upon men the face of your Christ, O Lord, do not turn it away, so that they may remain unhidden from his appearance, having been benefited. The cause of the certain fulfillment is the one having brought forth, saying, 'The Lord swore truth to David and will not deny it' [Ps 131:11].

The 'certainly shall be' regarding what was sworn in truth to David, concerning the coming of the Lord, is that the fruit of the womb of David shall sit upon his throne [Ps 131:11]. He will fulfill it as he swore; for the oath of God is truth, according to what was said by Gabriel to Mary concerning him being genealogically from David: 'And God will give him the throne of David his father, and he will reign over the house of Jacob forever' [Luke 1:32; Ps 131:12-13].

If someone takes the earthly Zion, how could he understand 'that my resting place for ever and ever' [Ps 131:14], since passing to the end of this age, the heaven and the earth pass away? For if the whole earth passes away, then the Zion which is upon the earth will also pass by. Regarding the spiritual Zion, concerning which it is written, 'Sing to the Lord who dwells in Zion' [Ps 87:1], that is the most holy Church, which he desired for a dwelling place for himself, he who said, 'I will dwell, what I have desired' [Ps 131:14].

Another [text] instead of 'the widow' says 'the huntress' and says: 'The unprotected and the brave guardian they do not have, I will bless all the poor to whom he provides an abundance of bread,' he says, 'I will fill her poor with bread' [Ps 131:15], since each of such poor people, being the seed of the righteous, is not diminished by bread. It is carried in copies as 'Blessing her huntress, I will bless.' And being blessed with the blessing of the Lord, she was a huntress hunting on every high mountain and...
translator_notes: True OET; Pass A ≠ Pass B. Melito skipped; never Cyril Matthew densify.

title: The Anointing and the Spiritual Dew
english: The sent-out fishermen and hunters in the crevices of the rocks are a symbol of those dwelling in the village of the hunters, for all dwell in Bethsaida, which is taken to be the village of hunters (Ps 149:9). 'I will clothe the priests of this Zion with salvation' (Ps 149:4). Christ has come as salvation for all, to seek and to save the lost (Lk 19:10). Regarding the presence of salvation and the clothing of it, it is written: 'Let my soul rejoice, for you have clothed me with a garment of salvation; they shall rejoice, and those who are holy of him shall rejoice in divine joy' (Ps 18:10).

There, in Zion, I will cause a horn to rise up for David (Ps 132:17). This horn of the kingdom is raised up by God in the house of David, according to what was said by the righteous: 'Raise up a horn of salvation for us in the house of David' (Ps 132:17). Prepare for this horn, Christ, who is found as a lamp, the Father running forward with his divine law for his visitation, for it is written: 'Your law is a lamp to my feet and a light to my paths' (Ps 119:105). And John, until the law and the prophets, is a lamp being prepared for his own Christ, concerning that Savior. There is that lamp which is kindled and shines: 'Did you not desire to rejoice at the right hour in his light?'

These things being theologized concerning the one who came from the seed of David according to the flesh, his enemies shall clothe themselves in shame, desiring, if they were consumed by fire, to say 'that a child was born, a son was given to us' (Isa 9:6), not recognizing the beginning of his time, mocking shame more, saying 'what he embraces with other men does not have a life that has ascended far above.' Therefore also upon him his holiness shall blossom, as it is said in Isaiah: 'And a flower shall ascend from the root' (Isa 11:1), following which the flowers of the earth shall appear in our land; such flowers being present toward the blossoming of the holiness by the Lord. For this blossoming sanctifies those passing by it, which is the very holiness of God, a flower, or rather to say, 'I am a flower of the field, a judge of the valleys' (Isa 35:1). If the flower and the judge of the field and of the valleys do not do these things, it is not fitting that flowers should appear in our land, once God has caused his holiness to rise up upon the enlightened and those approaching the...

A blessed and spiritual feast. The beard is a symbol of manhood. The oil descends from the beard of Aaron onto the shoulder of his garment (Ps 132:2). Aaron represents the shadow of priesthood. His head, the original, is filled with the divine oil of the name of Christ, regarding which it is said, 'Myrrh, your name.' This oil descends upon the beard of each who is able to say, after surpassing the shadow, 'I have become a man,' opposing the infant. Such a man becomes an imitator having become like Him, regarding which it is written, 'Behold, a man, whose name is Dawn, and a man comes after me' (Ps 133:1).

However, even if the oil descends upon Aaron's head, it does not descend upon a random beard but upon the high-priestly one, and from there onto the shoulder of the high-priestly garment. Aaron's tunic does not merely bear a type, for it is the Lord's body, born of the Holy Spirit, according to what was said concerning the Virgin: 'For that which was born in her is of the Holy Spirit' (Matt 1:18). Regarding the mountains of Zion, you shall perceive the divine and universal Church, which is the high doctrines of truth, the ornaments of the soul, having seized the being of Mount Zion (Ps 132:3).

Upon these mountains descends a spiritual dew, regarding which Moses said, 'And I will come down as dew' (Ex 16:4), and in the prophet, 'For the dew from you is its essence' (Hos 14:5). From this heavenly dew, the habitation of the blessed shall be from heaven. This spiritual dew does not descend from random clouds, but from the celestial light of the one saying, 'I have come as light into the world' (John 8:12). For this light both dews and shines from above, and makes [things] to become in most piercing brightness.

All the servants of the Lord bless the Lord (Ps 133:1), not having stepped far from Him but approaching Him through wisdom. Therefore they have stood in the court of the Lord, firmly established in Him. And they have stood in the courts of our God. The courts of God are where those who fear Him stand, the God-breathed writings and the doctrines of truth.
translator_notes: True OET; Pass A ≠ Pass B. Melito skipped; never Cyril Matthew densify.

title: The Nature of God and Divine Participation
english: It is not a temple for those ascending into it to follow the songs of the ascents and praise God joyfully. Therefore also 'Alleluia' is written upon the psalm, the superscription signifying that the living God must be hymned (Ps 134:1-3).

How will it not be that all those having ascended the ascents with songs and hymns will stand in the house of the Lord with right thought and unassailable practice, being His servants in the house of the Lord, and hymning Him in the courts of our God? But the courts of God are the old and new Scriptures, the theologies according to their parts, or the many dwellings in the promises in the house of the Father. And to praise first according to the introductions His name, so that they might serve the Lord and serve Him sincerely.

And toward allegory, if there are certain spiritual clouds, they signify a mental and invisible rain flowing. And these rise from the end of the earth, since the Gospel does not call those from great, rich, philosophical, oratory rulers, but from men thought to be the lowest, the unlettered and the laypeople. But He has also made the bright flashes of theories and the justices into a rain, to enlighten and to water those asking for these things in harmony with what is set forth. And He brings forth winds from their treasuries, which some signify better breaths and intellectual, transcendent natures.

This memorial is from the former generation of the Hebrews as a generation of the calling of the Gentiles, concerning which it is written, 'The coming generation shall declare to the Lord' (Ps 134:13b-14). And these things shall remain, as God has mercy on His people and calls upon His servants. For having responded to the intercession and the appeal of His servants on behalf of the people and themselves, being sent up, He was comforted, that is, He granted the appeal. Therefore also He has mercy on His people.

According to an upward leading, if in Israel there are those perceptive and seeing God with a pure heart, and in Aaron those who serve Him perfectly and priestly-wise continually, not day by day (Ps 134:19-21); and with these, the Levites are inferior to the sacred things, those being in the temple and the services being imposed in the...

Those who perform the service of the 251st God [Psalm 135] will not be newcomers to God, being brought into justice; and all those from foreign nations are added by the fear of the Lord. However, even if all bless, not each one will do this according to the proportion of power.

But those previously mentioned do not merely bless, but he is also blessed, not from a chance place but from the heavenly Zion, dwelling in the city of God, who gives the heavenly Jerusalem and the church which has no house or wrinkle, unlike Jerusalem, to see the peace which Jesus gives, saying, 'My peace I give to you' (John 14:27). But even if he is blessed in Zion by another thought, God is not thus in it and from it. Let these things also be said concerning the soul through knowledge and perfect virtue, being called Zion and Jerusalem.

The present psalm, being called forth for thanksgiving, commands to confess to the Lord, who does much in kindness and goodness (Ps 135:1-3). Therefore, in every verse, a hymn-like phrase is selected: 'For his mercy is unto the ages.' For since he neither ever has mercy nor ever does not, but always has mercy, it is fitting that those who hymn say, 'For his mercy is unto the ages.'

Of what gods is he, concerning whom it is said? If he is not God to them, then the Word of God did not become toward them according to the scripture saying, 'I am God' (John 8:58). For this one truly it is fitting to be called God; so do not worry even about those who are called gods around Abraham (Exodus 3:6; 'God of Abraham, and God of Isaac, and God of Jacob'; for this one truly it is fitting to be called God). According to this, the meaning of divinity and angels and divine powers is said to be 'gods,' as the apostle says, 'As there are many gods and many lords in heaven and on earth' (1 Cor 8:6), so all those called gods with the Trinity are such by participation of divinity.

But the Savior is not thus, but is God by essence; therefore he makes gods of those who partake of him. He has been said to be the only-begotten God; for he himself alone is the true God from the true God, being God according to the same nature as the Father, being consubstantial with the one who begets him.
translator_notes: True OET; Pass A ≠ Pass B. Melito skipped; never Cyril Matthew densify.
